{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — EXHIBIT 10.5 (Commerce One / Corio)

**Prepared for:** Customer-side deal team (we represent Corio, the customer/licensee)

## Executive summary

We have reviewed the Agreement against the playbook and verified 19 findings. The commercial architecture is broadly acceptable to us: there is **no exclusivity, non-compete, non-solicit, MFN, minimum-commitment or liquidated-damages obligation** binding Corio, the licences are perpetual, irrevocable and fully paid up, auto-renewal is exitable on 30 days' notice, and the Commerce One IP indemnity is uncapped (Section 9 excepts Section 8 from the fee cap). Those items sit at or above the fallback and we do not propose redlines.

Seven items require action. The most serious is **Section 13.5**, which reverses ownership of Corio-created Developments to Commerce One whenever Commerce One supports them on an ongoing basis, with no licence back — walk-away territory under our IP rule. **Section 9** narrows the liability cap to fees paid for "the transaction which the liability relates to" and carries no confidentiality, gross negligence or willful misconduct carve-outs. Other material gaps are the absence of any transition-assistance or data-export right on exit, the 60-day warranty period truncated by a December 31, 1999 outside date, mandatory AAA arbitration in place of a court forum, no affiliate licence extension, an unqualified assignment-consent right, no vendor insurance, and an audit notice with no minimum quantum.

One finding — **termination for convenience (Section 11)** — failed verification and is marked needs_review. The Agreement as drafted commits Corio to a five-year initial term with exits only for uncured material breach or insolvency, and no convenience right for us. The proposed new Section 11.4 has not been verified and should not be relied on or circulated until re-checked.

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant (at fallback) | § 8 INDEMNIFICATION. | IP defence/indemnity with standard remedy ladder; uncapped via the Section 9 carve-out. Preferred-only gaps (law/data-breach/wilful-misconduct heads, defence control) noted, not redlined. |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | **Deviation** | § 13 SHARED RESOURCES. | Ownership of Corio-created Developments reverses to Commerce One where it provides ongoing support, with no licence back; no embedded-IP licence, no Corio data-ownership statement, joint-development ownership open. |
| High | LOL-CAP — Cap, mutuality and carve-outs | **Deviation** | § 9 LIMITATION OF LIABILITY. | Cap narrowed to fees paid for the related transaction (not 12 months' fees); no carve-outs for confidentiality breach, gross negligence or willful misconduct. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Needs review (verification failed)** | § 11 TERM AND TERMINATION. | Five-year initial term; exits limited to uncured material breach and insolvency; no convenience right for Corio. Proposed Section 11.4 is unverified — re-check before use. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant (preferred) | SALES AND MARKETING COOPERATION | All grants nonexclusive; Exhibit D expressly non-binding; no sole-source or lead-with obligation on us. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Compliant (preferred) | § 9 LIMITATION OF LIABILITY. | No penalty, early-termination fee, shortfall or acceleration against Corio. § 4.4 audit true-up noted as compensatory only. |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant (preferred) | § 13 SHARED RESOURCES. | Only licence-scope and IP-protection limits bind us; § 13.6 preserves independent development. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | **Deviation** | § 8 7 WARRANTIES AND DISCLAIMER. | Warranty Period is 60 days from the Effective Date and capped at December 31, 1999 — below the 90-day software floor. Remedies otherwise meet the fallback. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | **Missing** | § 11 TERM AND TERMINATION. | No migration assistance or data-export obligation; § 11.3 covers only survival, continuing licences/support and return of Confidential Information. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | **Deviation** | § 14 MISCELLANEOUS. | California law acceptable at fallback; mandatory single-arbitrator AAA arbitration in San Francisco fails the fallback forum element. |
| Medium | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | **Deviation** | § 3 2. GRANT OF RIGHTS. | Successor transfer met via § 14.1, but no licence extension to Corio affiliates anywhere. |
| Medium | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | **Deviation** | § 14 MISCELLANEOUS. | Successor carve-out and consent requirement present, but consent carries no reasonableness standard and the successor carve-out has no notice mechanic. No CoC termination/re-pricing right. |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation burdening Customer | Compliant (preferred) | PRICING | No best-pricing, price-protection, disclosure or right-to-match obligation on Corio. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments / volume limits | Compliant (preferred) | § 4 FEES. | Fees track actual licences and usage; unlimited Software Users and Customers. Term length addressed under T4C, not double-flagged. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant (preferred) | § 13 SHARED RESOURCES. | No no-hire or anti-poaching covenant anywhere; personnel covenants bind Commerce One only. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant (fallback/preferred) | § 11 TERM AND TERMINATION. | 12-month renewals, 30-day mutual non-renewal notice, fees fixed for Year 2–5 and beyond. Absence of a vendor renewal reminder noted only. |
| Low | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | **Deviation** | § 4 FEES. | Once-yearly, independent CPA reasonably acceptable to us, records-only, Commerce One pays absent >5% underpayment; only "reasonable notice" sets no minimum quantum. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Missing** | § 14 MISCELLANEOUS. | No insurance covenant anywhere in the Agreement. |

## Walk-away items

1. **Section 13.5 — ownership reversal (IP, critical).** Where Commerce One supports the Developments on an ongoing basis, it retains all ownership rights in Corio-created work product with no licence back. Assignment of Customer IP to the Vendor is walk-away territory and also fails the fallback, which requires at minimum a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to the work product we lose. This must be resolved.
2. **Section 9 — per-transaction cap (LOL-CAP, high).** Limiting recovery to fees paid for the single related transaction can amount to a small fraction of 12 months' fees and risks falling below our walk-away floor. Treat the removal of the per-transaction narrowing as a condition of signature.

## Next steps

1. **Section 13.5 (IP):** delete the ownership-reversal carve-out so Corio owns Developments outright; add a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to Commerce One IP embedded in the Developments; add a sentence confirming Corio's data remains Corio's with Commerce One's use limited to providing the Software and services; confirm no IP is jointly owned.
2. **Section 9 (LOL-CAP):** delete the per-transaction narrowing so the cap is 12 months' fees, and add carve-outs for breach of confidentiality (Section 10), gross negligence and willful misconduct to the existing exception opener. Leave mutuality and the consequential-damages waiver untouched.
3. **Section 11 (T4C) — hold.** Re-verify before circulating. Our position remains a customer convenience right on 30 days' notice (fallback: 60–90 days) with a pro rata refund of prepaid fees and no reciprocal Commerce One convenience right during the initial or renewal terms.
4. **Section 11 (TRANSITION):** insert at least 90 days of transition assistance on any expiration or termination and export of our data within 30 days.
5. **Section 7 (WARRANTY):** extend the Warranty Period to 90 days and delete the December 31, 1999 outside date, which would otherwise contradict the extension.
6. **Section 14.3 (GOVLAW):** retain California law; replace mandatory AAA arbitration with exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in San Francisco County, and conform the Section 12.2 escrow cross-reference.
7. **Section 2 (LICENSE):** add a single provision extending the Section 2 licences to Corio's affiliates on written notice.
8. **Section 14.1 (ASSIGN):** add a reasonableness standard to the consent requirement and a written-notice mechanic for successor assignments; leave the mutual direct-competitor proviso and null-and-void sentence as drafted.
9. **Section 14 (INSURANCE):** insert the fallback clause (E&O USD 1,000,000; cyber/privacy USD 2,000,000), with the fuller CGL/workers' compensation/certificate version available if Commerce One prefers it.
10. **Section 4.4 (AUDIT):** fix minimum audit notice at 15 days; do not press the preferred refinements.

We suggest presenting items 1 and 2 as gating, items 4–6 as substantive but tradeable, and items 7–10 as clean-up in a single markup."}
